topics.label: Lecture introduction and objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the final lecture of the course and sets out the learning objectives for cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss traditional modalities for debulking and killing rapidly dividing cells alongside their associated toxicity and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic vulnerabilities and repair defects in cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how therapies can selectively eliminate tumour cells by taking advantage of their inherent regulatory defects and signalling dependencies.

topics.label: Small molecule kinase inhibitors and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: They cover the identification of driving oncogenes and the application, resistance pathways, and dosing strategies associated with small-molecule kinase inhibitors.

topics.label: Antibody-based targeted therapeutics
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the engineering and mechanisms of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates directed against cancer cell surface targets.

topics.label: Immune surveillance and checkpoint inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the role of the natural immune system against cancer and the mechanism of reawakening anti-tumour T-cell responses against neoantigens.

topics.label: Adoptive and engineered T-cell therapies
topics.groupedBecause: They explain cellular and molecular strategies that directly engineer or bridge T cells to target tumour-specific antigens.

topics.label: Current challenges and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: They reflect on overarching clinical obstacles, historical progress, and future strategies required to improve cancer survival.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and clinical dilemma in pediatric leukemia
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a historic success story in pediatric oncology to illustrate the ongoing ethical challenges in adopting new treatments.
